question.text: Should we try retrieval-aware conditioning for promoter expression prediction?

candidates.title: TabR: retrieval-augmented tabular prediction
candidates.claim: Neighbor retrieval can improve prediction when similar samples expose local structure.
candidates.risk: Naive retrieval can leak split information if neighbors are selected across evaluation boundaries.

candidates.title: GraphReg: modeling gene expression with regulatory graphs
candidates.claim: Graph-structured regulatory context can help connect distal elements to gene expression.
candidates.risk: May require high-quality regulatory edges that are unavailable or inconsistent across tissues.

context.baseline: 40kb promoter + distal-k8 lifted metadata + FiLM conditioning
constraints: main claims must use chromosome-aware split
new modules need ablation against the trusted baseline
promotion requires better Pearson without worse MSE/R2 consistency

evidence.title: TabR: retrieval-augmented tabular prediction
evidence.supports: Retrieval-style conditioning maps cleanly to tissue/sample-neighbor hypotheses.
evidence.cautions: Neighbor selection must respect chromosome-aware and gene-level boundaries. Context gate: chromosome-aware split.

evidence.title: GraphReg: modeling gene expression with regulatory graphs
evidence.supports: Graph priors align with enhancer-promoter regulation and distal context.
evidence.cautions: Requires reliable edge construction; start with diagnostic ablation before scaling. Context gate: chromosome-aware split.

plan.summary: Start with retrieval-aware conditioning because it has the clearest transfer path and testable leakage controls.
matrix: control: 40kb promoter + distal-k8 lifted metadata + FiLM conditioning
variant A: add retrieval features with train-split-only neighbor index
variant B: retrieval features with shuffled-neighbor negative control
variant C: remove new module while keeping preprocessing identical
stratify: report by chromosome, EID/tissue, and expression band
promotion_gate: MSE and R2 remain scale-consistent with the trusted baseline
sample-random gains are not used as main evidence
no neighbor or metadata lookup crosses evaluation boundaries
risks: Neighbor selection must respect chromosome-aware and gene-level boundaries. Context gate: chromosome-aware split.
Requires reliable edge construction; start with diagnostic ablation before scaling. Context gate: chromosome-aware split.
If gains only appear on sample-random split, mark as leakage-risk diagnostic.

cited_claims.claim: Recommendation 'promote to small controlled screen' is grounded in the transfer fit of TabR: retrieval-augmented tabular prediction.
Retrieval-style methods need split-aware neighbor controls before promotion.

review.reason: Promotion requires human approval before experiment execution.
required_actions: review cited claims and source refs
confirm main evaluation uses chromosome-aware split
confirm no retrieval, metadata, or graph lookup crosses evaluation boundaries
